transcript.text: I'm Steven Youngt and I live in Leilani Estates in Upper Leilani.
One day, I mean we're just living our life and you take the road Leilani Avenue in the middle of
the community to go to the beach and so we did and on the way back all broke loose,
the lava just started coming out of this street and then all of a sudden there's cracks everywhere
and we're like oh god that earthquake caused these cracks. Then steam starts coming out of some of
the cracks. The air was getting nasty, it was rocked by earthquake, kind of tremors, small ones and then
there was a big one, 4.2 was a fairly large one and that's the one that made the lava actually come
out of one in the crack in the middle of the street and we were just in shock. Nobody could believe
civil defense is our main source of knowledge you can trust because some people are doing fake
news on Facebook or something like that and it's important that people have something they can
believe in so civil defense doesn't tell us everything they only tell us what we need to know for safety
and for security so they're not going to tell us you know how far the lava is going today or something
but they're going to tell the people that live in its path that they better get ready and they better
and in Leilani they did a good job of getting us out of there when they felt that the situation was
unpredictable and I think they did a good job. If you have nowhere to go more and more people are
being evacuated as the lava is heading towards the ocean anybody that's in that area you know they're
going to have to have a place to go and so there's these disaster shelters that they started they did
first they did one in Pahoa and when it got pretty crowded then they opened one in Kao and then there's
people that are affected by Vogue which is the smoky volcanic ash and it has sulfur dioxide and
things in it and so they made one farther away at one of the churches sure foundation so there's
three places people that don't have any money can go and they feed you and they give you blankets
and water and whatever else you need and they provide some things that you need in order to sort
of camp out until this thing is over. The news is sensationalizing the event but with some reason
we want to make sure everybody here is safe but it doesn't affect about 90 percent of the people
that live on this island only about 10 percent live in the section that's affected and there
civil defense is in charge of making sure they're secure and that it's safe for everyone and they
tell us when to leave and stuff but I would say that it doesn't even affect most of the island
and it would be good for people to realize that the big islands open for business businesses like my
restaurant are you know really needing support right now and that it's perfectly safe right here
and it's even safer the farther you get away from the Puna district which is only one of seven
districts on the whole island.
